title: Lean verification of the Riemann Hypothesis

quotes.text: We hereby certify that both the statement and the proof of the Riemann Hypothesis are correct.
quotes.for: The communities certify both the theorem statement and its proof.

quotes.text: Joint statement by the Lean and Mathlib communities, endorsed by the Lean FRO and the Mathlib Initiative.
quotes.for: The joint statement is endorsed by the Lean FRO and the Mathlib Initiative.

quotes.text: On November 20, 2026, Levent Alpöge released a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis as a Lean library comprising 17 million lines of code.
quotes.for: Alpöge released the 17-million-line Lean library on November 20, 2026.

quotes.text: The codebase depends directly only on Mathlib. Over the past day, the Lean and Mathlib communities have rallied to verify the proof's correctness.
quotes.for: The library depends directly only on Mathlib.

quotes.text: By now, dozens of people have reported correct compilation of the codebase, reproducing the same raw proof export file.
quotes.for: Independent compilation reproduced the same raw proof export file.

quotes.text: The exported raw proof has been checked by several proof checkers, including Lean's official kernel, the con-leche and con-ron checkers, and several independent checkers.
quotes.for: The exported proof was checked by Lean's official kernel, con-leche, con-ron, and other independent checkers.

title: A remark on the Riemann Hypothesis

quotes.text: Claude and I have also formalized the arguments without assumptions.
quotes.for: Alpöge attributes the formalized argument to his collaboration with Claude.

quotes.text: Claude and I have had a great time together with such breadth in recent months, but this time Claude far outpaced me near the finish line.
quotes.for: Alpöge writes that Claude far outpaced him near the finish line.

quotes.text: In Stepanov's argument resolving Riemann over function fields one uses a divisor involving multiplicity. This argument is a descendant of Stepanov's, but multiplicity is hard to find over the integers
quotes.for: Alpöge describes the argument as a descendant of Stepanov's function-field proof.

quotes.text: The simple, new, Fourier-analytic ideas in the toy setting led us to examine chaining theta lifts if we were to have the same tricks recur but work in a natively automorphic manner.
quotes.for: Combining Fourier-analytic ideas from a toy setting with chaining theta lifts to work in an automorphic manner.

quotes.text: This puts us in the rather extraordinary situation this age has made possible, in which I am presenting the world with a complete argument before having mastered a massive neighbourhood around its mathematics.
quotes.for: Alpöge notes he is presenting the complete argument before mastering a large neighborhood around its mathematics.

quotes.text: I intend to do my best to understand and impart understanding of this argument and its certain simplifications, to speak about it, to write it properly.
quotes.for: Alpöge intends to understand, explain, and simplify the argument.

quotes.text: The precise timing is horrible. If I could have, I'd have finished this all much earlier.
quotes.for: Alpöge calls the timing of the release horrible.

title: Verification files for the Lean proof of the Riemann Hypothesis

quotes.text: The published Lean source compiles without errors, the five headline theorems depend only on the three standard axioms
quotes.for: Sutherland reports successful compilation and itemizes verification results.

quotes.text: Page last updated 2026-11-22 16:20 UTC. Results below are as of that time and this page will be updated as the remaining checks finish.
quotes.for: Sutherland's verification page was updated on November 22, 2026.

quotes.text: every module has been replayed through the Lean kernel, two independently written kernels, nanoda and con-leche, accept the full exported proof, and lean4lean accepts every compiled module.
quotes.for: Independent kernels nanoda and con-leche accepted the full exported proof, and lean4lean accepted every compiled module.

quotes.text: An independent sandboxed lake build of the archive reproduces the export byte for byte.
quotes.for: An independent sandboxed build reproduced the proof export byte for byte.

quotes.text: The lake comparator run and the Lean-kernel replay of the export are still in progress.
quotes.for: The lake comparator run and the Lean-kernel replay of the export remain in progress.

quotes.text: All 175,187 modules compile (Lean v4.33.1, Mathlib v4.33.1), pass, zero errors; finished 16:43:21 UTC.
quotes.for: All 175,187 modules compiled with zero errors under Lean v4.33.1 and Mathlib v4.33.1.

quotes.text: "GRH" here means Dirichlet L-functions: all moduli and all characters. Dedekind zeta functions, Hecke L-functions and automorphic L-functions in general are not among the statements that were checked.
quotes.for: The verified statements cover Dirichlet L-functions, not Dedekind zeta functions, Hecke L-functions, or general automorphic L-functions.

quotes.text: The Riemann hypothesis tells us about the deviation from the average.
quotes.for: The significance of the hypothesis for the distribution of primes.

quotes.text: Formulated in Riemann's 1859 paper, it asserts that all the 'non-obvious' zeros of the zeta function are complex numbers with real part 1/2.
quotes.for: Clay Mathematics Institute states that non-obvious zeros of the zeta function have real part 1/2.

title: Anthropic mathematician claims he used Claude to prove 19th-century Riemann hypothesis

quotes.text: He says that Claude helped develop a solution to the problem during the course of about six weeks.
quotes.for: Alpöge said Claude helped develop the solution over about six weeks.

quotes.text: Alpöge's note was published just one day after Anthropic went public on the Nasdaq stock market index.
quotes.for: Alpöge published his note one day after Anthropic went public on Nasdaq.

title: Alpöge/Claude proof of the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis

quotes.text: The Alpöge–Claude proof of the Riemann hypothesis explained for the Riemann zeta function (PDF, 164 pages; working draft, 21 November 2026).
quotes.for: Rubinstein released a 164-page working draft on November 21, 2026 explaining the proof for the Riemann zeta function.

quotes.text: A working guide to the proof, specialised to the Riemann zeta function, written with Claude, Codex and Gemini as an aid to studying it.
quotes.for: The working guide was written with Claude, Codex, and Gemini to translate the proof into classical analytic number theory.

quotes.text: It deduces the Riemann hypothesis from one inequality between weighted sums over primes, called (M), and two estimates for Dirichlet characters, and proves the two estimates from theorems in the literature.
quotes.for: The guide deduces the Riemann hypothesis from two Dirichlet character estimates proved from existing literature and one weighted prime-sum inequality taken from the Lean development.

quotes.text: That page records a check of the Lean proof run with Claude Code on University of Waterloo compute servers, starting from the archive Alpöge published.
quotes.for: Rubinstein also ran an independent check of the Lean proof on University of Waterloo compute servers.
